parts.t: Neighbourhood guide · City of Mission · Silverdale and the southwest
Mission-West is an MLS® sub-area name. The City of Mission doesn’t publish a boundary for it.
The City defines the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area in its Official Community Plan as a 3,440-acre area, and calls the area “sometimes known as Southwest Mission”.
On this site, listings tagged Mission-West are mostly on Nelson Street, Keystone Avenue, Silverdale Avenue, Clay Street, Gunn Avenue and Silverhill Avenue.
My working description, not an official boundary: Silverdale and the southwest of the city. My
covers Cedar Valley and the central streets.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 18, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate for 11+ years. Facts come from the official sources noted on this page. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Mission and Mission Public Schools (School District 75).
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations, flood rules and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: City of Mission Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area

parts.t: The City defines the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area in its Official Community Plan as a 3,440-acre area, and calls the area “sometimes known as Southwest Mission”
The City says the Central Neighbourhood Plan is the neighbourhood plan for the central part of Silverdale, and its Land Use Plan map is dated August 2022

blocks.text: BC Transit and the train Mission City Station

parts.t: BC Transit’s Central Fraser Valley route list includes Mission routes 31 Valley Connector, 32 West Heights, 33 Cedar Valley, 34 East Side, 35 Hatzic and 39 Shopper Shuttle

TransLink says the West Coast Express travels between Downtown Vancouver and Mission City on weekdays during morning and evening rush hours, westbound only in the mornings and eastbound only in the afternoon and evening
Mission City Station is at 33200 North Railway Avenue, and the buses that connect to it are operated by BC Transit

blocks.text: Fraser River edge ALR lands to the south

parts.t: The City says Agricultural Land Reserve lands along the Fraser River form the southern edge of the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area
The BC Government’s District of Mission Land Use Inventory (2011) records 1,539 hectares of Agricultural Land Reserve in Mission, close to seven percent of the District’s land area

blocks.text: Recreation, parks and the library for Mission-West

parts.t: From City of Mission pages and the City’s Leisure Guide, and Fraser Valley Regional Library. Street names are the City’s.

blocks.text: City recreation centre Mission Leisure Centre

parts.t: The City lists Monday to Friday 5:30 a.m. to 10 p.m., Saturday 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. and Sunday 7 a.m. to 9 p.m., with shorter hours on statutory holidays. Check the City’s status page before you go
The City’s upgrade page lists work on the leisure pool and hot tub, the main pool, a north arena, a curling arena, a weight room, a steam room and a sauna
Playgrounds for ages 0 to 5 and 6 to 12, tennis courts, a lacrosse box, outdoor fitness equipment, an off-leash dog area, paved trails, picnic tables, a washroom and a nine-hole disc golf course
The City says the Mission City Farmers Market runs there in the spring and summer, and the annual Lights On! Tree Lighting is held there

A Japanese Tea House is being developed in the park. The City’s project page gives the address as 7871 Taulbut Street and says construction is expected to begin in October 2026, with an opening event in early 2027
The City says the Activity Hub Master Plan covers the 20-hectare Centennial Park and Leisure Centre corridor

blocks.text: City parks Silverdale Park and Wren Park

parts.t: The City’s Leisure Guide lists Silverdale Park on Donatelli St. and Wren Park on Silverhill Ave.
The Leisure Guide is dated Fall 2023 / Winter 2024, so check the City’s current park pages
The Central Neighbourhood Plan recommends a new designation for the 273-hectare Silverdale Urban Forest, with over 24 km of dedicated forest trail
This is a recommended designation in a plan, not a built park
FVRL’s page lists Sunday 1 to 5 p.m., Monday to Thursday 9 a.m. to 8 p.m., and Friday and Saturday 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Hours change on holidays, so check before you go
It is the only FVRL branch in Mission, so there is no branch inside the Mission-West area

blocks.text: What to look at in a Mission-West home

parts.t: What the official sources say about the homes and lots, then the questions I go through with buyers.
The City describes the Silverdale Comprehensive Planning Area as designated for urban growth inside the urban growth boundary, planned as a complete community through the Central Neighbourhood Plan
A City information package for a Silverdale rezoning describes a proposal for approximately 45 townhomes as consistent with the Central Neighbourhood Plan land use designations

Lot size (MLS sales data, not an official source): the median lot size of detached houses sold between July 1 and October 8, 2026 was 68,738 sq ft, based on 6 sales with a recorded lot size. That is about 1.6 acres.

blocks.text: Planning and flood notes for Mission-West

parts.t: Plans, zoning and flood rules can be different for each lot.
The City adopted Official Community Plan Bylaw 6405-2026 on June 1, 2026. It replaces and repeals Bylaw 6350-2025, which the City’s public notice says is substantively the same plan.
The City’s Silverdale Master Infrastructure Strategy and the Central Neighbourhood Plan guide growth in Silverdale. The City dates the Central Neighbourhood Plan’s Land Use Plan to August 2022.
The Stave Heights Neighbourhood Plan was adopted into the Official Community Plan on May 16, 2022, and Council endorsed the Stave Heights Engineering Plan on October 3, 2022.

The City describes the Stave Heights plan area as an “environmentally sensitive hillside landscape”, and its plan sets Protected Natural Asset areas measured from the top of bank of watercourses, in most cases 15 m.
The City says the Activity Hub Master Plan covers the 20-hectare Centennial Park and Leisure Centre corridor.
The City lists a Fraser River flood preparedness and response plan among its plans.
I found no City page that gives a floodplain designation for specific streets in this area.
The BC Government’s District of Mission Land Use Inventory (2011) records 1,539 hectares of Agricultural Land Reserve in Mission, close to seven percent of the District’s land area.
